name: TRUNC
description: TRUNC truncates a number to an integer, or to a specified number of decimal places, by removing digits without rounding.
tldr: Truncates a number to an integer or set number of digits (no rounding).

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value you want to truncate.

parameters.name: num_digits
parameters.description: The number of decimal places to keep. 0 (default) truncates to an integer.

basicExample.explanation: TRUNC removes the fractional part without rounding, so 4.9 becomes 4.

advancedExamples.title: Negative numbers truncate toward zero
advancedExamples.description: Unlike INT, TRUNC does not round down.
advancedExamples.explanation: TRUNC simply drops the fractional part, giving -4 (whereas INT(-4.9) = -5).

advancedExamples.title: Keep two decimal places
advancedExamples.explanation: TRUNC keeps 3.14 and discards the remaining digits without rounding up.

howItWorks: TRUNC chops off digits beyond the specified number of decimal places; it does not round. With num_digits = 0 it returns the integer part toward zero. For positive numbers TRUNC and INT give the same result, but for negatives TRUNC moves toward zero while INT moves toward negative infinity.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: TRUNC only removes digits; it never rounds, which differs from ROUND.
For negative numbers it truncates toward zero, unlike INT which rounds down.
num_digits can be negative, truncating to the left of the decimal point (e.g. TRUNC(1234, -2) = 1200).

commonErrors.fix: Use ROUND if you need rounding instead of truncation.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: TRUNC works identically in Google Sheets.

faq.question: What is the difference between TRUNC and INT?
faq.answer: TRUNC removes the fractional part toward zero (TRUNC(-4.9)=-4), while INT rounds down (INT(-4.9)=-5).

faq.question: Does TRUNC round?
faq.answer: No. It simply cuts off digits. Use ROUND if you need rounding.

faq.question: Can num_digits be negative?
faq.answer: Yes. A negative num_digits truncates to the left of the decimal, e.g. TRUNC(1234, -2) = 1200.
